deed: שלושה ישראלים פיתחו שיטה להוכיח זהות בלי לחשוף את הסוד עצמו
title: Researchers at the Weizmann Institute developed a way to prove identity without revealing the secret itself

trailer.text: Uriel Feige, Amos Fiat and Adi Shamir, of the Department of Applied Mathematics at the Weizmann Institute of Science in Rehovot, Israel, are the authors of the paper Zero-knowledge proofs of identity.

According to Feige, Fiat and Shamir, the problem with most current identification methods (ID cards, credit cards, computer passwords, PIN codes and the like) is that the person being identified proves his identity by revealing a constant secret value, in the form of a printed card or a value remembered by heart.
Anyone who copied the card or recorded the secret can impersonate him later.
Fiat and Shamir described a scheme in which a user proves his identity to any other user, without shared or public keys.
According to the paper, the prover convinces that he knows his secret without revealing the secret or even any partial information about it.

stations.title: A secret revealed with every use

paragraphs.text: According to Feige, Fiat and Shamir, a card, a password and a PIN work the same way: the person being identified proves who he is by revealing a constant secret.
This secret can be a printed card or a value memorized by heart.
According to the paper, an adversary working with a dishonest verifier can copy the card or record the secret, and then impersonate the person being identified.

Fiat and Shamir's paper gives examples from real life: credit card numbers can be copied to blank cards or used over the phone, computer passwords are vulnerable to hackers and wiretappers, and terminals of military command and control systems may fall into enemy hands.
Credit card numbers can be copied to blank cards or used over the phone.
Computer passwords are vulnerable to hackers and wire tappers, and military terminals may fall into enemy hands.
According to the paper, passports are another example, because hostile governments inspect and photocopy them.
According to the paper, the problem is particularly challenging when the prover and the verifier are adversaries, and the aim is that the verifier cannot impersonate the prover.

stations.title: At the Weizmann Institute in Rehovot

paragraphs.text: Amos Fiat and Adi Shamir wrote the paper How to Prove Yourself at the Department of Applied Mathematics at the Weizmann Institute of Science in Rehovot.
They presented it at the CRYPTO '86 conference, and it was published in 1987 in the LNCS 263 series.
According to the paper, their scheme combines two things: interactive zero-knowledge proofs that already existed (by Goldwasser, Micali and Rackoff, 1985), and identity-based schemes.
According to the paper, its main contribution is to show that such protocols are relevant to practical identification and signature problems.
The authors thanked Mike Fischer, Oded Goldreich, Shafi Goldwasser, Silvio Micali, Charlie Rackoff, Claus Schnorr and Avi Wigderson for many of the ideas in the paper.
According to the textbook, a trusted center chooses two secret prime numbers, p and q, and multiplies them into a number N.
Only N is distributed to all users.
According to the paper, unlike RSA, only the center knows which primes the number is made of, and therefore everyone can use the same number.
According to the paper, the center can be a government or a credit card company, and it issues smart cards after properly checking the user's physical identity.
Before that, the center prepares a string with the user's details: name, address, ID number, physical description and security clearance.
According to the paper, the security of the scheme rests on the difficulty of extracting modular square roots when the factorization of n is unknown.
According to the textbook, the user proves that he possesses secret information, without revealing it.

stations.title: Zero knowledge: not even one bit leaks

paragraphs.text: In 1988 Feige, Fiat and Shamir published a slightly different version of the scheme.
According to the paper, Fiat and Shamir's earlier scheme leaked only one bit.
According to the abstract, the paper defines zero-knowledge proofs of knowledge: the prover shows that he knows something without revealing any computational information, not even that one bit.
The authors explain this with a parable, which they themselves say is not technically accurate.
According to the parable, a person can convince that he is a mathematical superstar without revealing anything new about the problem.
According to the paper, in this version the trusted center only publishes a number n, which is the product of two large primes.
After publication the center can be closed, since it has no further role.

According to the paper, in the "keyless" version of the scheme, in which the trusted center (which knows the factorization of n) issues smart cards to users, and assuming the cards are built with tamper-resistant technology, the zero-knowledge property guarantees that no information leaks, and therefore users of the system gain no advantage in trying to copy or forge smart cards.

stations.title: Fast and small enough for a smart card

paragraphs.text: According to the paper's abstract, typical implementations require only 1% to 4% of the modular multiplications RSA requires.
According to the paper, in one setting the average number drops to 7.6 multiplications, compared with 768 multiplications in RSA.
For signing, after arranging the multiplications, 32 multiplications are required, only 4% of an RSA signature.
According to the paper, in one setting the proof exchanges 323 bytes, and the secret fits in a 320-byte ROM.
For signing, the private key is stored in 576 bytes, and each signature takes 521 bytes.
According to the paper, a related protocol by Fischer, Micali and Rackoff was presented at the Eurocrypt 84 conference, and the new protocol is faster than it and requires less communication.
According to the paper, for the same level of security, a number of rounds equal to the square root of the previous number is enough.
According to the abstract, thanks to its simplicity, security and speed, the scheme is especially suited for smart cards, personal computers and remote control systems.
An unlimited number of users can join without harming the system, and there is no need to keep a list of all users.
One verification device can check many types of personal, financial and occupational cards from different organizations.
According to the paper, if the chance of a successful forgery is one in a million, and the card costs one dollar to manufacture, each success will cost the forger about one million dollars.
At a national-security level of security, an adversary who tries 1000 times a day is expected to succeed only once in 3000 years.
According to the paper, the level of security can be changed even after the key has been chosen.
According to the abstract, the schemes are provably secure against any known or chosen message attack, if factoring is difficult.
The signature is provably secure under the same condition, even if it is not zero-knowledge.
Uriel Feige and Adi Shamir of the Weizmann Institute in Rehovot also wrote a paper on witness hiding and witness indistinguishable protocols.
According to them, a witness hiding protocol does not reveal the prover's secret, and anyone who does not know the secret cannot impersonate him.
According to Feige and Shamir (1990), the original proof that the parallel version of the identification scheme is secure required detailed number-theoretic analysis.
In their paper this security follows as a special case of a general theorem.
According to the 1986/87 paper, when the rounds of the proof are run in parallel, the protocol is no longer zero-knowledge, for technical reasons.
Even so, it can be formally proven secure.
According to the 1988 paper, parallel execution saves communication rounds, but is not zero-knowledge for subtle technical reasons.

According to the paper, message authentication with this scheme is not a real signature, because a judge who did not participate in the interaction cannot later decide whether the message is authentic.
The authors also write that practical implementations, with particular moduli and pseudorandom functions, may still be vulnerable to specialized attacks.

unknowns.text: The pages do not say whether the scheme was actually used in smart cards or passports, only that it is suited for them according to the paper
The claims state the Weizmann Institute in Rehovot, Israel, as the workplace of the three researchers, but not their citizenship

claims.text: לפי פייגה ושמיר (1990), פרוטוקול זיהוי שמסתיר עד אינו חושף את העד של המוכיח, ואיש אינו יכול להתחזות למוכיח אם אינו מכיר את העד שלו.
claims.quote: The WH identification protocol never discloses P's witness, and nobody can misrepresent himself as P unless he really knows P's witness

claims.text: לפי פייגה ושמיר (1990), ההוכחה המקורית לאבטחת הגרסה המקבילית של סכמת זיהוי המבוססת על העלאה בריבוע מודולו מספר פריק דרשה ניתוח תורת־מספרים מפורט, אך האבטחה היא מקרה פרטי של משפט 4.1.
claims.quote: The original proof of security of the parallel version of this scheme involved detailed analysis of its number theoretic properties, but in fact the security of the protocol is just a special case of Theorem 4.1.

claims.text: לפי מאמר 1986/87, הגרסה המקבילית של הפרוטוקול אינה אפס־ידע מסיבות טכניות, אך אפשר להוכיח את אבטחתה באופן פורמלי.
claims.quote: This version is not zero-knowledge for technical reasons, but its security can be formally proven by the techniques developed in Section 3.

claims.text: לפי המאמר, הרצות מקביליות מפחיתות את מספר החלפות כיוון התקשורת, אך הן אינן אפס־ידע מסיבות טכניות עדינות.
claims.quote: Parallel executions change the direction of the communication only a constant number of times (which is preferable for theoretical as well as practical reasons), but unfortunately they are not zero knowledge for very subtle technical reasons.

claims.text: לפי המאמר, אימות הודעה בשיטה הזו אינו חתימה אמיתית, כי שופט שלא השתתף באינטראקציה לא יכול להחליט אחר כך אם ההודעה אותנטית.
claims.quote: but this is not a real signature scheme: without participating in the interaction, a judge cannot later decide if a message is authentic.

claims.text: לפי המאמר, מימושים מעשיים עם מודולים ופונקציות פסאודו־אקראיות מסוימות עלולים עדיין להיות פגיעים למתקפות ייעודיות.
claims.quote: Practical implementations which use particular moduli no and psuederandom functions fo may still be vulnerable to specialized attacks
